children: Indonesia is set to enter 2027 with relatively resilient growth momentum, with the economy forecast to expand 4.9%, BMI says in a note. However, Indonesia remains vulnerable to shocks from food, oil prices and financial markets, it says. A severe El Nino could push inflation to 5.3% and slow growth to 4.2%, it adds. Rising food costs could reduce household purchasing power and consumer spending, drive up food imports and require additional government support. A renewed oil-price shock would pose the biggest threat to Indonesia's fiscal and external balances, while a potential MSCI downgrade could trigger capital outflows and weaken the rupiah, it adds. Both scenarios could prompt tighter monetary policy and slow economic growth, although a weaker rupiah would help improve the current account, BMI says. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
